abstract.para: A move constraint is a location constraint used specifically for moving a resource. The cluster creates the move constraint automatically when you move a resource with &crmsh; or &hawk;.

listitem.para: The resource doesn't have any other constraints that would prevent it from moving.
You can perform this procedure on any node in the cluster.

step.para: Log in either as the &rootuser; user or as a user with sudo privileges.
Check which node the resource is currently running on:
Move the resource to another node:
Alternatively, you can move the resource away from the current node without specifying a specific node to move to:
Check the status again to make sure the resource is now running on the other node:

listitem.para: You can use &hawk; on any machine with a Web browser and network access to the nodes.

step.para: In a Web browser, go to https://HAWKSERVER:7630/ and log in.
From the left navigation bar, select Monitoring Status.
Find the resource you want to move. In the Operations column, click the down arrow button and select Migrate.
From the drop-down list, either keep the default Away from current node or select a specific node to move the resource to.
The node in the Location column changes, and a link icon appears in the Status column. Hover the cursor over the link icon to see the name of the move constraint.
